title: Prayers for My Wife
lede: Original prayers from U.S.M.C. Ministries. Put your names in, and carry it in your pocket or print it for the nightstand.

items.title: Her Worth
items.body: Father, thank You for {{wife}}. Before I ask You for one thing, let me say plainly that she is a gift I did not earn and could not have arranged. Teach me to speak of her worth where other men can hear it, and to believe it in the quiet hours when no one is listening. Let her never have to wonder what I think of her.

items.title: Her Rest
items.body: Lord, {{wife}} carries more than I see. Show me the weight she is holding that she has never named out loud, and let me take some of it off her without being asked and without making a speech about it. Give her real rest tonight, and make our home a place where rest is possible.

items.title: My Tongue Toward Her
items.body: Father, guard my mouth in my own house. Kill the sarcasm I have learned to hide behind. Let the last thing {{wife}} hears from me tonight be something she can lean on tomorrow. When I am tired and short, let me choose the harder, kinder word.

items.title: When I Have Wounded Her
items.body: Lord, when I have hurt {{wife}}, do not let me settle for a fast apology that protects my comfort. Give me the kind of sorrow that changes a man. Let me name the thing I did without excuse, without blaming her reaction, and without needing the matter closed on my schedule.

items.title: Her Faith
items.body: Father, grow {{wife}} in the knowledge of Your will. Let her walk with You in a way that does not depend on my leadership being good that week. Give her roots of her own, and let me be glad — never threatened — when she knows You better than I do.

items.title: Our Oneness
items.body: Lord, You made us one flesh, and I have lived too many days as though we were roommates with a shared calendar. Restore what distraction has thinned out. Give us conversation that goes past logistics and a friendship that outlasts the season of raising children.

items.title: Her Body and Health
items.body: Father, I ask for {{wife}}'s health — her body, her sleep, her strength. Where she is worn down, restore her. Where there is pain she has learned to work around, bring healing. And let me notice before she has to tell me.

items.title: Her Fears
items.body: Lord, meet {{wife}} in the fear she does not say out loud. Be near her at two in the morning when her mind will not stop. Let her know that she is held by You, and let me be a man whose steadiness makes it easier for her to believe it.

items.title: Against Bitterness
items.body: Father, pull up any root of bitterness in me before it grows into something our children inherit. Where I have kept a record of {{wife}}'s wrongs, let me burn the record. Where she has reason to keep one of mine, make me safe enough that she does not need it.

items.title: Her Calling
items.body: Lord, {{wife}} is not only my wife — she is Your servant with work of her own. Show me what You have given her to do, and let me clear the ground for it instead of crowding it out. Let her strength and dignity be something our home is built to hold.

items.title: Purity and Loyalty
items.body: Father, I make a covenant with my eyes. Let no image, no screen, no second look steal what belongs to {{wife}}. Keep me faithful in the dark, in the hotel room, on the phone at midnight. Let my loyalty be a fact and not a claim.

items.title: Growing Old Together
items.body: Lord, give us years. Let me still be glad in {{wife}} when the house is quiet and the children are gone. Keep affection alive in us, and let the last chapter be warmer than the first.
